scope: Claim-level IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, scouting, threshold, control, pesticide-law, CAPA, and program-audit evidence for THC-ENC-321 through THC-ENC-340.
rules: Generic greenhouse and institutional IPM guidance supports methods and decision structure but does not create universal Cannabis efficacy thresholds.
Pesticide and disinfectant use remains governed by current labels, registrations, worker-safety requirements, residue rules, and jurisdictional law.
All mappings remain pending independent science review.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Integrated pest management is a decision system that prioritizes prevention, monitoring, correct identification, context-specific thresholds, and lower-risk controls before escalation.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: IPM categories and thresholds are context-dependent; these sources do not establish universal cannabis economic thresholds or pesticide permissions.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Clean-to-dirty movement, separation of propagation/intake areas, and controlled personnel/material flow can reduce opportunities for pest and pathogen movement through a facility.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Facility layout and movement controls reduce risk but do not guarantee exclusion; organism biology, compliance, and local workflow remain material.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Incoming plants can introduce pests or latent pathogens, so intake inspection, quarantine, source records, and testing are distinct biosecurity controls.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Quarantine duration and testing frequency cannot be universalized across pests, pathogens, source risk, crop stage, and facility design.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Personnel, clothing, footwear, and work sequence can move contaminated material, making entry controls and clean-area-first workflow relevant to biosecurity.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: The importance of each personnel pathway is organism- and facility-specific; hygiene measures must remain compatible with worker-safety requirements.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Tools, benches, containers, and propagation surfaces can serve as contamination or transmission pathways, and sanitation works best when soil and organic debris are removed before disinfection.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Sanitation efficacy depends on organism, surface, cleaning quality, product, concentration, contact time, and label directions.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Cleaning physically removes soil and organic matter, while disinfection applies an appropriate antimicrobial process to a cleaned surface; the two steps are not interchangeable.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: A disinfectant cannot compensate for poor surface preparation, and no one chemistry is universally compatible or effective for every organism or material.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Disinfectant performance depends on preparation of the surface and achieving the labeled concentration and wet contact time under compatible conditions.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Contact time and concentration are product-specific label requirements, not generic cannabis recipes.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Irrigation water, reservoirs, recirculating solution, and wet root-zone systems can move or maintain plant pathogens, so water-system hygiene belongs in disease prevention and trace-back.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Reservoir detection or wet conditions do not prove a specific plant disease; organism-specific diagnostics and validated treatment methods remain necessary.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Screens, sealed openings, protected intake points, and controlled doors can reduce pest entry, but exclusion design must account for pest size and ventilation penalties.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: No universal mesh size or sealing specification fits every pest, structure, climate, or airflow requirement.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Humidity, leaf or flower wetness, airflow, drainage, and temperature can change disease-favorable conditions and therefore belong in preventive environmental management.
claimEvidence.sourceLocator: See registered source(s) for the scoped IPM, biosecurity, sanitation, diagnostic, legal, or quality-system evidence described in this record.
claimEvidence.applicability: Supports the lesson-level mechanism and decision workflow while keeping crop, pest/pathogen, facility, measurement, regulatory, and local operating context explicit.
claimEvidence.limitations: Environmental risk factors alter probability but do not diagnose a pathogen or establish a universal cannabis setpoint.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Repeatable scouting routes, plant-part inspection, traps where appropriate, spatial records, and consistent counting methods support trend detection better than ad hoc observations.

claimEvidence.limitations: Trap counts and selected-plant observations are samples rather than whole-crop censuses; interpretation depends on route, device, crop stage, and pest behavior.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: When symptoms overlap or management consequences are material, diagnosis should escalate from observation to representative sampling and organism-appropriate laboratory methods.

claimEvidence.supportedClaim: Biological control depends on matching the beneficial organism or microbial agent to the target, life stage, environment, timing, and compatibility with other IPM tactics.
